title: Silas and the Ghost
premise: Vesper Sterling, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Group—an embassy that exists on no map—has spent nine years erasing other people's problems. When Flight 447's records vanish mid-flight and the plane lands carrying a passenger who died in 1998, Vesper discovers the ghost is a product of the same black program that trained him, now selling memory-wipe technology to the highest bidder. Hunted by his own handlers and haunted by erased memories of a sister he never knew he had, Vesper must burn the network from inside, choosing found family over the only identity he has left. In the end, he trades his own records for theirs, becoming officially no one—and finally, privately, someone.
about_author: Oscar Quintana is the pen name of a former logistics consultant who spent a decade working contracts he still can't discuss. He writes thrillers from a coastal town in Portugal, where he keeps, out of habit, a go-bag by the door.

chapters.title: The Polished Lie
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. A routine cleanup—scrubbing a diplomat's affair—establishes Vesper's world: the Meridian Group, his go-bag, his meticulous lies. His handler, Ilsa, hints something big is coming. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness; Vesper trusts procedures more than people, and the reader feels the cost of that.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Every digital trace of Flight 447 evaporates while it's airborne—manifests, radar, even passengers' phone histories. Vesper is ordered to meet the landing quietly. Among the disembarking passengers is a man whose death certificate is twenty-six years old. Beat: dread blooming under professional calm.

chapters.title: The Passenger
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Vesper and the dead man, Tomas Reyes, who remembers nothing after 1998. Vesper realizes Tomas's memories were surgically restored—and that the technique matches gaps in Vesper's own past. Beat: uncanny recognition; the ghost is a mirror.

chapters.title: Ashfall Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Meridian orders Tomas terminated and Vesper to do it. Instead Vesper hides him with Nadia Okafor, a disgraced archivist who once tried to expose the program. First betrayal by the institution he served. Beat: the vertigo of switching sides.

chapters.title: What the Archive Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia. In a decommissioned data vault, Nadia finds the Ashfall files: a training program that wiped recruits' families to make them loyal. Vesper's file lists a sister—alive until three years ago. Beat: grief for a family he never mourned because he never knew it existed.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Hallway
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Meridian's kill team finds them; a brutal escape through Lisbon's flooded aqueduct costs them their safehouse and nearly Nadia. Ilsa catches Vesper alone and offers him reinstatement if he delivers Tomas. Beat: temptation—the old lie almost fits again.

chapters.title: The Sister's Room
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. He visits what was his sister Marta's apartment, kept untouched by her found family—a queer chosen household who welcome this stranger who looks like her. Through their stories, Vesper inherits a life. Beat: warmth as revelation; found family shown before it's threatened.

chapters.title: Counterweight
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The team turns Ashfall's own wipe technology against its architects, seeding the network with poisoned archives while Meridian closes in. Ilsa reveals she trained Vesper—and chose to keep one memory intact: Marta. Beat: fury and gratitude braided together.

chapters.title: Burn the Network
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Climax at the Ashfall facility: Vesper broadcasts the entire program—names, clients, methods—to every intelligence service at once, then faces the director who erased his childhood. He spares him, letting exposure be the execution. Beat: catharsis through refusal to become the weapon he was made to be.

chapters.title: No Records
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Months later: Meridian dissolved, Tomas rebuilding a life from borrowed decades, Nadia publishing under her own name. Vesper, officially nonexistent, sits down to dinner at Marta's old table with her people. He unpacks the go-bag for good. Beat: quiet resolution—inheritance accepted, memory chosen over erasure.
